Changes, all in `ledger/ledger.py`:

- **Freezing** is a set of frozen ids alongside the balance dict. `freeze`, `unfreeze`, and `is_frozen` each check the account exists first. Withdrawals and outgoing transfers on a frozen account raise `PermissionError`, while deposits and incoming transfers are unaffected. Closing an account also drops it from the frozen set.
- **Single transfers** now delegate to a private helper that validates and applies one transfer against whatever balance mapping it is handed.
- **Batch transfers** run every transfer through that same helper against a scratch copy of the balances, then swap the copy in only after all succeed. Any failure raises before the swap, so the live ledger is untouched. Transfers within a batch are applied in order, so a later transfer can spend funds received by an earlier one.

On the side note: I did not switch to an operation log. The codebase is built on snapshot state, and copy-then-commit gives the same all-or-nothing guarantee in a few lines without changing the source of truth or making reads slower. If replay or an audit trail becomes a requirement later, that would be the point to reconsider event sourcing as a deliberate migration rather than a side effect of this feature.
